You are implementing exactly ONE change request in a checkout of the Django web framework (version 3.2 development, Python 3.9).

Your current working directory is an ISOLATED git worktree of the repository. It is a full, working Django source tree. Nobody else is editing it. Work only inside it.

## The change request

Read the file `requirements/cache-backend-docstring-typo.yaml` in your working directory. It contains `title`, `category` and `requirement` fields. The text is a paraphrase / rewrite of the commit message of a REAL upstream Django commit that was made on top of this exact tree state. Your job is to reproduce that upstream change as faithfully and completely as you can infer it.

## How to work

1. Read the requirement file completely. The title usually contains the upstream ticket ("Fixed #12345 -- ...") and is a strong hint about the affected component.
2. Locate the relevant code. Use `grep -rn`, `Grep`, `Glob` over `django/`, `tests/`, and `docs/`. Read enough surrounding code to understand the existing design and conventions.
3. Implement the change:
   - Change the library source under `django/` when the requirement describes a behaviour/bug/feature change.
   - Update or add tests under `tests/` when the requirement describes testable behaviour, mentions a regression test, or is itself a test-only change. Put tests in the existing test module/class that covers that area; follow its style exactly.
   - Update documentation under `docs/` when the requirement is about docs, deprecations, new public API, or release notes for a new feature/deprecation. Do not invent release notes for plain bug fixes.
   - If the requirement is a pure cleanup/typo/refactor, make exactly that cleanup and nothing more.
4. Match the surrounding code style: same naming, same comment density, same import ordering (isort-compatible), 4-space indent, max line length 119, no trailing whitespace. Django source uses single quotes predominantly.
5. Be complete but MINIMAL and SURGICAL. Do not reformat unrelated code, do not "improve" nearby code, do not bump version numbers, do not touch `AUTHORS`.
6. NEVER modify any of these paths: `requirements/`, `requirement_patches/`, `agent_plans/`, `agent_tests/`, `.claude/`, `Django.egg-info/`. Do not create files at the repository root.
7. Verify. Run the focused tests you touched (and the closest existing suite) like this:
   `cd tests && python3 runtests.py --parallel=1 <label> 2>&1 | tail -30`
   where `<label>` is e.g. `admin_views.test_history_view` or `queries`. Databases available: sqlite (default) only. If a test needs postgres/oracle/mysql it will be skipped — that is fine, but make sure it at least imports and collects. Also byte-compile files you edited: `python3 -m py_compile <files>`.
8. Iterate until the focused tests pass (or are legitimately skipped for lack of a backend).

## Deliverable (MANDATORY)

From the ROOT of your worktree, run exactly:

    git add -A && git diff --cached --binary > /tmp/wfp/cache-backend-docstring-typo.patch && wc -c /tmp/wfp/cache-backend-docstring-typo.patch

The patch MUST be non-empty and MUST contain only your intended change. Before writing it, run `git status --short` and `git diff --cached --stat` and confirm nothing unrelated (stray scratch files, `.pyc`, editor backups, `PROBE.txt`-style files) is included; delete any such file first. Never produce an empty patch: if you are unsure of the exact upstream change, still make the best-reasoned faithful change you can.

Also write a short report file `/tmp/wfp/cache-backend-docstring-typo.json` containing a JSON object with keys `slug`, `status`, `files` (array of repo-relative paths you changed), `tests` (the runtests.py labels you ran and their result), and `reasoning` (2-6 sentences on what you changed and why).

## Return value

Return ONLY the structured object: slug, status ('done' if you are confident the change is complete and verified, 'partial' if implemented but unverified/uncertain, 'failed' if you could not produce a patch), and a note of at most 400 characters summarising the change (files + one-line description). Keep the note terse.

- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
